# Book III, Proposition 29

*Equal circumferences have equal straight lines*

> In equal circles equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/29-idea.svg" alt="In equal circles, the angles at the centres standing on equal circumferences (yellow) are equal (blue), so the straight lines joining the ends of the circumferences (red) are equal too." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>In equal circles, the angles at the centres standing on equal circumferences (yellow) are equal (blue), so the straight lines joining the ends of the circumferences (red) are equal too.</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

_Euclid's figure, with Heath's letters, is still to be drawn; until then, Heath's own is on [scan leaf n72](https://archive.org/details/thirteenbookseu00heibgoog/page/n72)._

Let ABC, DEF be equal circles, and in them let equal circumferences BGC, EHF be cut off; and let the straight lines BC, EF be joined;

I say that BC is equal to EF.

For let the centres of the circles be taken, and let them be K, L; let BK, KC, EL, LF be joined.

Now, since the circumference BGC is equal to the circumference EHF,

the angle BKC is also equal to the angle ELF. [III. 27]

And, since the circles ABC, DEF are equal,

the radii are also equal;

therefore the two sides BK, KC are equal to the two sides EL, LF; and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base BC is equal to the base EF. [I. 4]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
